sections.summary: Inventory filters are Pinterest's advertiser-facing brand safety controls for understanding the content that appears near ads.

claims.text: Brand safety inventory filters help advertisers understand what kinds of content will appear near their ads on Pinterest.

evidence.locator: Inventory filters: These filters help you to understand what kinds of content will appear near your ads. You can look specifically at exposure level for your campaigns

claims.text: Advertisers can look specifically at the exposure level for their campaigns and see how Pinterest policies impact those settings.

evidence.locator: Inventory filters: These filters help you to understand what kinds of content will appear near your ads. You can look specifically at exposure level for your campaigns and see how policies impact those settings.

claims.text: Pinterest incorporated inventory filters directly into its ads management tools in 2024.

evidence.locator: 2024 - Added third-party brand safety measurement solutions with trusted partners - Incorporated brand safety inventory filters directly into our ads management tools

sections.summary: Pinterest describes what the filters show but not the exact serving logic behind them.

claims.text: The filters surface the exposure level of a campaign — the kinds of content appearing near its ads — and show how Pinterest's policies affect those settings.

evidence.locator: Inventory filters: These filters help you to understand what kinds of content will appear near your ads. You can look specifically at exposure level for your campaigns and see how policies impact those settings.

claims.text: Because the filters describe exposure levels and policy impact, they appear to function primarily as visibility/reporting controls over adjacent content rather than a guarantee that specific content will never appear next to an ad.

evidence.locator: Inventory filters: These filters help you to understand what kinds of content will appear near your ads...

claims.text: Inventory filters sit alongside other Pinterest brand safety controls — placement opt-out, keyword exclusion, Performance+ targeting opt-out, and third-party measurement via IAS and DoubleVerify — rather than replacing them.

evidence.locator: Our partnerships with IAS and DoubleVerify give you more options for brand safety reporting...

sections.summary: Best suited to advertisers auditing the content environment around their Pinterest ads.

claims.text: Use it when you need to understand, before or during a campaign, what kinds of content will appear near your ads and at what exposure level.

evidence.locator: Inventory filters: These filters help you to understand what kinds of content will appear near your ads. You can look specifically at exposure level for your campaigns

claims.text: Use it when you want to check how Pinterest's content policies affect the inventory your campaigns are exposed to.

evidence.locator: You can look specifically at exposure level for your campaigns and see how policies impact those settings.

claims.text: Do not rely on it when you need hard exclusion of specific publishers or search queries — Pinterest points to placement opt-out and keyword exclusion as the controls for restricting where ads appear.

evidence.locator: Inventory filters: These filters help you to understand what kinds of content will appear near your ads...

sections.summary: Pinterest confirms the filters live in Pinterest's ads management tools but does not document a step-by-step setup path.

claims.text: Inventory filters are available within Pinterest's ads management tools, having been incorporated there in 2024.

evidence.locator: 2024 - ... Incorporated brand safety inventory filters directly into our ads management tools

claims.text: Pinterest states advertisers can customise many brand safety settings within campaign settings, so checking campaign settings in ads manager is a reasonable starting point.

evidence.locator: You can customise many settings within campaign settings

sections.summary: No vendor uplift figures are provided; KPI guidance below is inferred from the documented exposure-level mechanism.

claims.text: A useful KPI to watch is the campaign's content exposure level: if the filters show high exposure to unsuitable content categories, tightening adjacent controls (placement opt-out, keyword exclusion) could conditionally reduce unwanted adjacency — with the trade-off that restricting placements typically narrows reach and may raise delivery costs.

evidence.locator: Inventory filters: These filters help you to understand what kinds of content will appear near your ads. You can look specifically at exposure level for your campaigns

claims.text: Brand safety scores against industry standards and suitability categories, available through IAS and DoubleVerify partnerships, are a reporting-based KPI that complements the filters' exposure view.

evidence.locator: Our partnerships with IAS and DoubleVerify give you more options for brand safety reporting. These trusted partners can help you to take a closer look at brand safety levels and how your campaigns score against industry standards and various brand safety and suitability categories.

sections.summary: Cross-platform alternatives are listed with their material differences.
Single official source used throughout the guide. Source checked: 2026-11-17.

claims.text: Pinterest Business Help — Brand safety on Pinterest: https://business.pinterest.com/en-gb/brand-safety/

evidence.locator: Better brand safety controls for advertisers on Pinterest

relationships.name: Content suitability in Performance Max
relationships.difference: Google's Content Suitability Center sets inventory type (Maximum, Moderate, Limited) for YouTube, Display Network and Google Video Partners, and its channel exclusions cannot be applied at ad group or campaign level; Pinterest's inventory filters instead let advertisers view exposure levels for their campaigns and how policies impact them.
relationships.context: Both address brand suitability in automated/simplified campaign experiences, but Google's control is inventory-type selection for YouTube/Display/Video Partners, while Pinterest's filters focus on understanding exposure levels near ads.

evidence.locator: "Target the right inventory type at the account-level (YouTube, Display, Video Partners)" — Maximum/Moderate/Limited inventory
evidence.source_title: How to use brand suitability features in Performance Max

relationships.name: Inventory filter for in-content ads
relationships.difference: Meta's inventory filter lets advertisers set the sensitivity level of content their in-content ads appear next to, specifically Facebook in-stream reels and ads on Facebook Reels; Pinterest's inventory filters are described as helping advertisers understand exposure levels near their ads rather than setting a sensitivity level for named placements.
relationships.context: Both are advertiser controls over the content adjacent to ads on a social platform, but Meta's applies to specific in-content placements while Pinterest's is a campaign-level exposure view.

evidence.locator: "**In-content ads** (Facebook in-stream reels and ads on Facebook Reels)"

relationships.name: Brand safety options (Smart+)
relationships.difference: TikTok's Smart+ brand safety options are chosen when setting up placement in the upgraded Smart+ experience; Pinterest's inventory filters instead help advertisers understand what content appears near ads and at what exposure level.
relationships.context: Both are brand safety options surfaced during campaign setup, but TikTok's is a placement-time choice in Smart+ while Pinterest's filters are about exposure visibility.

evidence.locator: "You can additionally choose brand safety options."
evidence.source_title: How to create a campaign in the upgraded Smart+ experience

relationships.name: Publisher block lists
relationships.difference: Meta's publisher block lists let advertisers block ads from appearing adjacent to specific publishers for Facebook reel in-stream ads; Pinterest's inventory filters are described as an exposure-level understanding tool, not a publisher-level block list.
relationships.context: Both relate to controlling ad adjacency, but Meta's blocks named publishers while Pinterest's filters describe exposure levels.

evidence.locator: you can use the following brand suitability controls to help you place ads adjacent to content and publishers that are more suitable for your brand: inventory filter, publisher block lists
evidence.source_title: About Facebook in-stream ads for Reels

relationships.name: Search Ads brand safety settings
relationships.difference: In TikTok Search Ads, advertisers review placement settings at ad group level and choose brand safety settings; Pinterest's inventory filters instead surface exposure levels for campaigns and how policies impact them.
relationships.context: Both are brand safety settings chosen at ad group/campaign setup, but TikTok's Search Ads settings are placement choices while Pinterest's filters are exposure reporting.

evidence.locator: Placements and brand safety: Review placement settings and choose brand safety settings for the ad group
evidence.source_title: Set up a Search Ads Campaign

relationships.name: Brand exclusions
relationships.difference: Google's brand exclusions are a campaign-level control to exclude brands and prevent overlaps with unwanted queries; Pinterest's inventory filters help advertisers understand content exposure near ads rather than excluding specific brands or queries.
relationships.context: Both are campaign-level brand safety controls, but Google's excludes brands/queries while Pinterest's filters are about content exposure visibility.

evidence.locator: FAQ list of campaign-level controls: "Brand exclusions"
